extracted.intended_audience: researchers, industry and academic teams seeking to engage with or apply for DARPA STO programs/opportunities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for teams proposing research, technology development, or transition efforts to DARPA's Strategic Technology Office (STO), describing the office mission, thrust areas, technical interests, and types of engagement sought. Useful for shaping proposals to align with STO priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: trusted, disruptive capabilities across physical domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop technology to give national security leaders trusted, disruptive capabilities to win in all physical domains — air, space, sea, and land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STO's work spans the spectrum of competition, from deterrence to high-end combat. Proposals should aim to deliver capabilities that are both trusted and disruptive across one or more physical domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope across competition spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should span the spectrum of competition, from deterrence to high-end combat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects may be targeted at peacetime competition, escalation deterrence, or high-end combat applications; proposers should state where on this spectrum their effort applies and how it supports mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage key enabling technologies (microelectronics, computing, ML/AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage advancements in microelectronics, computing capacity, applied machine learning/artificial intelligence, and other technologies to create advantages for U.S. forces and blunt adversarial strengths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should show how they exploit or advance these enabling technologies to produce operational advantage or mitigate adversary capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic impact across multiple national realms
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower the nation to assert dominance in realms of diplomacy, information, military, economy, finance, intelligence, environment, and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should articulate how their work contributes beyond purely tactical effects — e.g., effects on information, economic, or diplomatic dimensions — and the broader national-security implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrust Area — Advanced Active and Passive Sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop novel technology and methods to find, detect, track, and follow difficult and elusive objects of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should leverage sensing technologies including radio frequency, acoustic, and electro-optic/infrared across all domains to create broad networks that leave adversaries with 'nowhere left to hide.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrust Area — Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance systems to achieve and counter kinetic and non-kinetic effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas of interest include acoustics, directed energy, electronic and cyber warfare, photonics, and strategy analysis using modeling and simulation. Proposals may address either offensive/enablement or counter-capability approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrust Area — Command, Control, and Communications (C2/C3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create technologies and concepts to empower human decision making and execute command and control with minimal communications in a highly dynamic threat environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STO is interested in innovations for complexity management, decision aids, distributed autonomy and teaming, human behavior modeling, and resilient communication networks. Proposals should emphasize adaptability, resilience, and reliability under constrained communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrust Area — New Paradigm of Systems Warfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape the balance of power and enable protracted engagements in contested environments through autonomous systems, technologies, and concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address common operational constraints such as limited communications, power, weight, adaptability, and cost; emphasize sustained effectiveness in contested, degraded, or denied conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thrust Area — Critical Capabilities to Promote National Resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop capabilities to provide advantage in expanding areas, such as commercial lunar infrastructure and protection of critical infrastructure at home and among allies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STO seeks efforts that leverage advanced technologies to examine commercial, financial, and industrial infrastructure and ensure resilience of national systems including energy, transportation, and communication services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical topic interests (complexity management, autonomy, human behavior modeling, networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Areas of particular STO interest include complexity management, decision aids, distributed autonomy and teaming, human behavior modeling, and communication networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals addressing these topics should show technical novelty and operational relevance; explicitly connect proposed research to STO thrusts and expected mission impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of engagement STO supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to engage include R&D programs and efforts, challenge competitions, and technology transition efforts for the Strategic Technology Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should consider which engagement mechanism best fits their maturity and transition plan (e.g., a short challenge vs. a multi-year program) and plan for transition to users where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program character: finite-duration, high-risk/high-reward, transition-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: STO research programs are finite in duration, but the revolutionary advancements they drive create lasting change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be designed as time-bounded efforts with ambitious technical goals and clear pathways to transition and operational impact; emphasize revolutionary potential and transitionability.
